graphs.title: A bigger temperature rise means more heat released.
graphs.label: Heat released

experiment.aim: To find the heat released when an acid is neutralised by an alkali
experiment.hypothesis: The bigger the temperature rise, the more heat is released
controlled: Specific heat capacity of the solution

steps: Set the rise to 3 °C and press Record.
Set the rise to 6 °C and press Record.
Set the rise to 10 °C and press Record.
Compare the heat for each rise.
title: Heat of neutralisation
goal: Work out the heat released from the rise in temperature.
note: The heat released is taken up by the solution: Q = m c (change in temperature). Here the solution has a mass of 100 g and a specific heat capacity of 4.2 J/(g °C).
